steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how has your skin been since your acne care with us? I usually hear one of three things. My skin has stayed clear, it's starting to break out again, or I'm breaking out like before. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Skin Has Stayed Clear
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes treatment with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still happy with the results.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

steps.title: Starting to Break Out Again
steps.content:
I'm sorry they're coming back, {{contact_first_name}}. Breakouts can return after care stops. It's not anything you did wrong. What kept you from coming back in?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Breaking Out Like Before
steps.content:
I'm sorry, {{contact_first_name}}. I know that can be hard. Breakouts can come and go, even after skin clears. What changed before they came back?

(Let them answer. Be kind. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, can I ask you a few quick questions about anything else you've noticed?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Transition: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to the breakouts. First, can I ask a few quick questions so your file is current?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every concern they name. You'll recap them in a moment.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few skin concerns people often notice. Just let me know which ones apply to you, even if they're mild or come and go.

Are you having any breakouts now?

Any breakouts along your jawline or chin?

Are dark marks staying after breakouts clear?

Have you noticed any scarring or pitting?

How about oily skin or large pores?

Any breakouts on your back or chest?

Are you seeing any redness?

Do your products feel like they're not working?

Do you feel like you have to cover it with makeup?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every concern they name, including the first one.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few skin concerns people often notice. Just let me know which ones apply to you, even if they're mild or come and go.

Are you having any breakouts now?

Any breakouts along your jawline or chin?

Are dark marks staying after breakouts clear?

Have you noticed any scarring or pitting?

How about oily skin or large pores?

Any breakouts on your back or chest?

Are you seeing any redness?

Do your products feel like they're not working?

Do you feel like you have to cover it with makeup?

(Recap everything, including what they mentioned first, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, between these, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask about {{main_concern}} so your file is current.

(Ask these questions in order. Pause after each.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a few weeks, or more like months?

(Let them answer. If it fits, you can say "Got it.")

Is it something you notice now and then, or every time you look in the mirror?

(Let them answer. If it fits, you can say "I see." or "I understand.")

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with photos, going out, or feeling put together?

(Let them answer. If they name an impact, reflect only what they said; if they mention photos, you might say "You notice it in photos." If none, you can say "Got it, thank you.")

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Read back their three answers: how long, how often, what it gets in the way of.)

So it's been on your mind a while, and you notice it most times you look in the mirror. At its worst it gets in the way of what you mentioned. Did I get that right?

(Say what they named: photos, going out, or feeling put together. Let them answer. If they correct you, take the correction and move on.)

It sounds like you'd like to feel comfortable with your skin again. Is that fair to say?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If we can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Uncover the Real Concern
steps.content:
Okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm not going to push you on it. What's the part giving you pause?

(Let them answer. Then tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Why Did They Stop?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad your skin has stayed clear.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in?

(Let them answer. Do not argue with it.)

Breakouts can creep back after care stops. A skin check lets us see how things are going. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for a skin check. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “It cleared up and then came right back”
steps.content:
That's frustrating, {{contact_first_name}}, and it's not a sign you did anything wrong.

Can I ask, did it come back in the same place, or somewhere new, like the jawline?

(Let them answer.)

Acne isn't one thing. Breakouts that return in the same place usually mean the plan stopped before the skin settled. Breakouts in a new place often mean something changed, like stress or hormones. Either way, it's information about {{main_concern}} that we didn't have last time.

{{provider_name}} can look at it now and adjust instead of starting from zero.

Would it help to know which one it is?

steps.title: Objection: “I didn’t see enough of a difference”
steps.content:
I appreciate you telling me, {{contact_first_name}}. That's worth hearing.

Can I ask, how long did you give it before you stopped?

(Let them answer. Do not promise results on the call.)

Skin turns over about once a month. Most acne plans need two or three of those cycles before the change shows. Stopping in the middle can look like it didn't work. Your notes show exactly what was done, so we're not guessing.

{{provider_name}} can look at {{main_concern}} today and hear what you were hoping for. Then you'll hear plainly whether it was the timing or the plan.

Is that worth one visit to find out?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m embarrassed it’s back”
steps.content:
Please don't be, {{contact_first_name}}. Nobody here is keeping score.

Can I ask, was it one thing that got in the way, or did it just drift?

(Let them answer. Stay warm.)

Breakouts come back for most people once a plan stops. That's how skin behaves, not something you did. The only thing embarrassment does is keep people away until it's a bigger job than it needs to be. With scarring, waiting has a cost.

{{provider_name}} would rather see you now than a year from now. We'd take a look at {{main_concern}} and figure out the shortest path back.

Would it feel better to just get that first step done?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m not sure it’s worth it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask, is that about the cost, or about whether you'd see a change?

(Let them answer. If it's cost, use the cost answer.)

Worth it comes down to one question, and it's whether {{main_concern}} is still bothering you. If it is, it's been bothering you for a while now, and it hasn't sorted itself out. Breakouts you leave alone don’t just clear. They leave marks, and marks are harder to treat than breakouts.

{{provider_name}} can look at where things stand and tell you plainly what's realistic. If the answer is that it's not worth it for you, you'll hear that too.

Would knowing that be worth one short visit?

steps.title: If They Say: “My skin was clear”
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}. When skin is clear, coming back can stop feeling important. Breakouts can return slowly after care stops.

Does that make sense?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they name another reason, go back and tap it.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back in for a skin check. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: Cost or Budget
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. A skin check is just a chance to look. You're not committing to anything.

Does that seem fair?

(Let them answer.)

(Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they name another reason, go back and tap it.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “Life got busy”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up, and skin checks get pushed down the list. We can work around your schedule.

Would that work?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they name another reason, go back and tap it.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's find a time that's easy for you. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “I’ll come back when the breakouts return”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Breakouts can start small before they're easy to notice. A skin check lets us see how things look now.

Does that sound right?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they name another reason, go back and tap it.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for a skin check. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: They Moved or Tried Another Provider
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change. If you're nearby, we'd be glad to see you again. Your skin history is still in your file.

Would that be okay?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they name another reason, go back and tap it.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m considering another option”
steps.content:
That's fair. Can I ask what you're looking at, like a dermatologist, a prescription, or another office?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other option.)

Those can all make sense, and some people do well combining them. The part that's hard to compare from home is what would move {{main_concern}} for you. {{provider_name}} already knows how your skin responded last time, so you're not starting over here.

Come in, get a straight answer on where things stand, and then compare. If the other option turns out to be the better fit, you'll be choosing it for a reason.

Is that a fair way to decide?

steps.title: Objection: Cost
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it the cost of the visit itself, or the thought of paying for a full plan again?

(Let them answer. Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

This first visit is one appointment, not a plan. You'll hear what anything past that costs before you decide on it. And since you've been here before, we're not starting from scratch, and starting from scratch is the expensive part.

The other side of it is what {{main_concern}} is already costing you, the things you mentioned a minute ago. That's the part I'd hate to see keep adding up.

Can we at least get the look on the calendar?

steps.title: Objection: “I don’t have time”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it finding time for the first visit, or the worry about a run of visits like before?

(Let them answer.)

Right now we're only talking about one visit. {{provider_name}} looks at {{main_concern}} and tells you what it would take from there. Sometimes that’s a small change to what you’re doing. Sometimes it’s a short series, and you’ll hear that up front so you can decide. Nobody is booking you into a series on the phone.

We'll fit that first visit around your schedule, not the other way around.

Could you find a short window for that?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to talk to my spouse”
steps.content:
Of course. Is it more about the money side, or do you two just make these decisions together?

(Let them answer. If it's money, use the cost answer.)

That's fair, and I'm not asking you to commit to anything they'd need to weigh in on. Right now, all you can tell them is that {{main_concern}} is on your mind. After the visit, you can tell them what's going on and what it would take. That's an easier conversation to have. And if they'd like to come along, they're welcome.

Can we pencil it in, and you can move it after you two talk?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Usually when someone says that, there's one specific thing on their mind. What's the part you'd want to think over?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

Okay. I'm not trying to rush you. The one thing I'd say is that {{main_concern}} is on your mind. It's been that way for a while, and it hasn't sorted itself out on its own. The visit is how you get the information you'd be thinking with. You can think it over just as easily after you know what's going on.

Would it be easier to think it over once you have the answers?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I can do that, {{contact_first_name}}. What would you want it to cover, so I send the right thing?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

I'll be straight with you, though. Anything I send is going to be general. It can't tell you what's realistic for {{main_concern}} specifically. That takes {{provider_name}} looking at your skin, and that's one short visit.

Let's do both. I'll send the information, and we'll put a time on the calendar. If what I send answers your question, you can call and cancel, no problem.

Does doing both work for you?
